description: Replaces one passage of an existing wiki page without resending the body. Pass the exact text to replace (oldString) and what it becomes (newString) — the same contract as a code editor's Edit: oldString must occur **exactly once** on the page. If it is missing, or occurs more than once, nothing is written and the error says which; copy the text verbatim from get_wiki (whitespace and line breaks count) or include more surrounding text to make it unique. newString="" deletes the passage. Matching is literal, not a regex. This is the normal way to fix a sentence, update a value, or correct one rule on a page that already exists. Use write_wiki when you are composing a page or rewriting several sections at once, and mode="append" there when a section is genuinely missing. The edit is a revision like any other write: it folds into your previous write within 30 minutes unless newRevision=true, and baseRev refuses the edit when the page moved on since you read it. The response carries rev, coalesced, previousBodyChars and bodyChars, plus warnings[] when the page as a whole now strays from the skeleton — not the body. Requires a write-scope token.

baseRev.description: The revision you read. If the page has moved past it, the edit is refused.

newRevision.description: Force a new revision instead of folding into your last write.

newString.description: The replacement text. "" deletes the passage.

oldString.description: The exact text to replace. Must occur exactly once on the page.

page.description: Page slug of an existing page.

name: edit_wiki
title: Change one passage of a wiki page
